title: Caucasian Iberia
capsule: The Kingdom of Kartli (Caucasian Iberia; Georgian: ქართლის სამეფო) was founded c. 302 BCE by Pharnavaz I, the progenitor of the long-lived Pharnavazid dynasty, on the territory of present-day eastern Georgia with its capital at Mtskheta. The kingdom occupied a geopolitical hinge between Rome and Parthia—later Sasanian Persia—and around 317 CE King Mirian III adopted Christianity as the state religion following the mission of St. Nino, making Kartli one of the earliest Christian kingdoms. Internal conflict and Sasanian pressure led to a period of Persian client kingship, and in 580 CE the Sasanian emperor Hormizd IV abolished the monarchy and appointed a marzpan (governor), converting the kingdom into a Persian province. Iberia's cultural and dynastic legacy passed to the subsequent Principality of Iberia and ultimately to the unified Georgian monarchy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core territorial extent in eastern Georgia is well established through Georgian chronicles (Kartlis Tskhovreba), Greco-Roman geographic sources, and numismatic evidence, though precise borderlines with Colchis and Caucasian Albania fluctuated.
